A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEV uncertainty benchmark and UFCE framework. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite retitling and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, calibration, misclassification and OOD detection experiments on CARLA, nuScenes and Lyft, including ablations and repeated-initialization results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments and additional Simple-BEV, corruption, OOD-selection and hyperparameter-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The Dirichlet evidential model, UFCE loss, uncertainty-dependent weighting and pseudo-OOD KL regularization are retained. Vacuity Scaling is renamed Epistemic Uncertainty Scaling with the same equation. Simple-BEV is an additional evaluation backbone, without a new proposed algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The original datasets and segmentation tasks remain. v2 adds nuScenes-C evaluation covering seven reported corruption types at three severities, alternative semantic OOD configurations involving barriers and kangaroos, and a camera-segmentation-to-BEV uncertainty experiment. These substantially broaden tested input conditions and OOD populations.

E2.justification: The five principal uncertainty-method families remain; Vanilla/Entropy and Evidential/ENN are matched renamings. However, the nuScenes ablation replaces UFCE and UFCE-ER controls with UCE and UCE-ER, and qualitative comparisons replace component-ablation comparators with ENN-UCE, Energy, Dropout and Ensemble (v1 Figures 5–7; v2 Figures 4–6).

E3.justification: Reported focal/CE learning rates change from 4e-4/1e-4 to 4e-3/1e-3, and generic grid-search reporting becomes sequential tuning against validation pseudo-OOD AUPR. v2 adds Simple-BEV configurations, FPR95 evaluation and clean-to-corrupted testing. Timing hardware changes from A100 to A6000 for inference. These documented changes do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analyses for all three proposed hyperparameters, alternative-OOD transfer tests, corruption robustness, CARLA town/weather breakdowns and camera-to-BEV uncertainty analysis. It restructures the nuScenes ablation and removes the standalone Lyft ablation and earlier qualitative component-ablation figure.

E5.justification: The three-random-initialization study and its numerical uncertainty entries are identical in v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 24. Ensemble initialization and dropout-pass counts also remain unchanged; no new confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Many nuScenes and Lyft scores are replaced. For example, full-framework nuScenes LSS IoU changes from 0.374 to 0.356 and OOD AUPR from 0.313 to 0.335 (v1 Tables 1/5; v2 Tables 1/2). These are revised results under changed reported settings, not established same-setting gains. Extensive new results accompany the added analyses; road-segmentation scores are retained after unit conversion.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–5 and the Appendix A.1 derivations retain the same substantive assumptions and arguments, including the UFCE closed form, entropy bound and gradient analysis. Changes are principally notation and numbering. Added standard metric formulas explain existing metrics rather than introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The benchmark and UFCE contributions remain central. v2 expands the benchmark claim to three architectures and emphasizes calibration and uncertainty estimation while maintaining segmentation accuracy. Its conclusion also broadens the superiority claim to aleatoric uncertainty and calibration, whereas v1 emphasized segmentation improvement and OOD detection.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of pseudo/true-OOD similarity, regularization tradeoffs, corruption-related failures and environmental variation. Appendix A.2.2 explains possible camera-to-BEV uncertainty distortion and distinguishes semantic OOD detection from domain-shift robustness. These substantially expand the interpretation of applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, explicit tuning ranges and selection criteria, Simple-BEV implementation settings, ten-bin ECE reporting, OOD masking instructions and OOD pixel ratios. These substantially extend v1's reproducibility documentation, although the general batch-size statement conflicts with the specific Simple-BEV setting.

R1.justification: Related-work positioning expands substantially through a new Appendix A.2.2 covering structured-data uncertainty, camera segmentation, BEV calibration, robustness and downstream applications. Discussions of Ancha et al., MapPrior, RoboBEV and other added works explain distinctions and adaptation challenges beyond v1's backbone and uncertainty-method summaries.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. UCE background is relocated, its limitations receive a dedicated subsection, scaling is renamed and integrated into the framework section, and experimental and appendix material is reorganized into targeted subsections.

P2.justification: Tables are substantially redesigned with separate method rows, FPR95 columns and colored ranking highlights. CARLA and road tables move to the appendix; new sensitivity, dataset and robustness tables are added. Gradient plots are redrawn, qualitative panels are replaced, and the document adopts a different conference layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of generalization beyond v1's default OOD pairings. Alternative-pair and corruption tests expose performance limits, while sensitivity studies and clearer tuning/access information improve interpretability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, although some new claims overstate their tables: the Simple-BEV discussion claims best OOD AUROC, but Table 16 reports 0.845 for Ours versus 0.914 for ENN-UCE.
